newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra canvasses new Sydney airport options.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra canvasses new Sydney airport options.

text.p: Australian Transport Minister John Sharp on Wednesday published possible plans for Sydney's new airport, including three runways for both possible sites.
Sharp released two configurations for each of the two airport sites -- Holsworthy in Sydney's south-west and Badgerys Creek beyond the western urban fringe.
Each of the plans showed one or two very long, 4,000 metre (13,100 foot) runways, which would be among the longest in any of the world's airports.
The second parallel runway, if not 4,000 metres, would be 3,600 metres (11,800 feet) or 3,800 metres (12,500 feet) long, the plans showed.
Australian international airports tend to have long runways to safely accommodate Boeing 747s at the very great take-off weights necessary for maximum range.
The new airport, at whichever site, would also have a third, cross runway 2,500 metres (8,200 feet) long.
The plans showed the new airport would have rail connection, with the rail station under terminals between the main runways.

The former Labor government selected Badgerys Creek as the site for Sydney's second airport but the new Liberal-National government, elected last year, is examining Holsworthy, a former army firing range that is much closer to the city centre.
But the main Sydney airport for the indefinite future is expected to be the existing one in the inner suburb of Mascot, just 15 minutes by road to the city centre.
